plain_text:
FITCHBURG PUBLIC LIBRARY
BOARD OF TRUSTEES
Minutes October 14, 2026
Fitchburg Public Library
166 Boulder Drive, Suite 108, Fitchburg MA
Trustees present were: Chair Matthew Bruun, Sabrina Holley-Williams, Mary Rice Hurley, Joanne Huse, 
Cynthia Jones, Muna Kangsen, Eric Mbunwe, Dennis Pierce, and Jim Walsh. Also present were Director 
Deb Hinkle and Assistant Director Jean Tenander.
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order at 6:33 p.m.
PUBLIC COMMENT
 There was no public comment.
APPROVAL OF THE MINUTES
The Minutes of the Sept. 16, 2026 Trustees Meeting were approved.
CHAIR’S REPORT
Chair Bruun reported that the city approved the appropriation in the full amount of the MBLC 
Pandemic Eescalation Payment to the Building Project. 
Jim Walsh mentioned the recent news article in the Fitchburg Sentinel about the new library.
LIBRARIAN’S REPORT
Director Hinkle said she had submitted the annual financial report required in order to receive 
state aid to the MBLC.
She said the vacant pre-professional position had been internally posted this week.
Parking issues have been problematic recently. Neither contractors nor sub-contractors have been 
permitted to park in the Boulder Drive lot. With permission from the Mayor, the library staff has been 
permitted to park around the perimeter of the lot across Newton Place (behind The Arc). The issue of staff
and patron parking once relocated back to 610 Main Street is still being discussed. The former staff 
parking lot space has been lost to the footprint of the renovated and expanded building.
The new mascot Wallace will debut at Trick or Treat on Main Street on Saturday October 24.
Director Hinkle said the Children’s Department and Teen Department plan to partner with 
Fitchburg Public Schools 21st Century After School Program next summer through a Massachusetts 
Department of Education grant, a federally funded competitive grant program to provide programming 
during Out-of-School Time. Grants are awarded competitively for up to three to five years. There is a 
potential to get a bus route from the High School to the Library.
There are several opportunities for a Cultural Council grant to support Library programming this 
year.
Director Hinkle said the FSU Community Read this year is Project Hail Mary by Andy Weir. 
There will be a reading aloud event at the Fitchburg Library on Friday November 10 at 12pm. The 
Director thanked Marcia Ladd for all the work she has done on the project over the years.
The Friends of the Library Nancy Project will begin on the Saturday after Thanksgiving. The 
Friends are also participating in the Trick or Treat on Main Street event. 
COMMITTEE REPORTS
Eric Mbunwe is the newly appointed Treasurer. Jim Hohman has made funds available to transfer
in preparation for the Trustee donation to the OWL Capital Campaign.
BUILDING COMMITTEE
The contractors have completed more painting and interior work. The Building Committee 
reported the furniture vendors are not changing their prices despite schedule changes. Almost all the glass
is in place. Joanne Huse said she would like a Trustee tour. The Director will schedule one for November.
Although the larger campaign goal has been reached, the OWL Capital Campaign’s Legacy of 
Learning book spine program will continue.
POLICIES COMMITTEE
Dennis Pierce reported that the Policies Committee had met this month. He suggested the 
Committee work on policies relating to the new building first. He said the next ones under consideration 
would be policies relating to the Makerspace and our internet policy. He suggested Trustees take the 
proposed draft home and prepare questions for the next meeting. He asked whether the MBC would look 
over proposed policies. Muna Kangsen suggested having the city legal department review the policy as 
well.
OLD BUSINESS
There was no Old Business.
NEW BUSINESS
There was no New Business
ADJOURNMENT
The meeting adjourned at 7:22 p.m.
Respectfully submitted by
Jean Tenander for
Cynthia Jones
